official.deadline_note: Scholarship application window runs 1 December 2026 to 15 January 2027; results announced 1 April 2027. Required documents must reach University Admissions by the document submission deadline - the scholarship page states 2 February while KTH's general 'How to apply' page states 1 February.
official.application_cycle: For studies starting in August 2027 (opens 1 Dec 2026, closes 15 Jan 2027)
official.status_note: The foundation is awarding one scholarship in 2027. Application opens 1 December 2026 and closes 15 January 2027; scholarship results are announced 1 April 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The KTH India Scholarship covers the tuition fee for the first and the second year, provided that the study results during the first year are satisfactory. KTH's fees page states the full tuition fee for most two-year programmes with both years spent at KTH is SEK 385,000, but it varies between the programmes.
benefits: The KTH India Scholarship covers the tuition fee for the first and the second year, provided that the study results during the first year are satisfactory.
The scholarship also includes a monthly living allowance during the academic year (10 months).
The foundation is awarding one scholarship in 2027.
Please note that Indian citizens are eligible to apply for both the KTH India Scholarship and the KTH Scholarship.
Applicants from Mumbai Metropolitan Area and Pune will be prioritized according to the foundation's statutes.
eligibility: To be eligible for the scholarship you must be a fee-paying student and have applied for a master's programme at KTH as your first priority and paid the application fee.
You cannot apply for or be awarded a scholarship for programmes listed as your second, third or fourth priority.
You must also be an Indian citizen who has completed your undergraduate programme in India.
Students with conditional eligibility also qualify.
The scholarship is not available for applicants to joint master's programmes or programmes with obligatory exchange studies, such as the master's programme in Railway Engineering.
Academic qualifications from an internationally recognised university equivalent to a Swedish bachelor's degree.
requirements: Only applicants who fulfil the admission requirements of the programme applied for are eligible for a scholarship.
English proficiency equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6/English Level 2.
Documents submitted in the application to University Admissions must be submitted by the document submission deadline.

application_method: Before applying for the KTH India Scholarship, you must first apply for a master's programme at KTH via universityadmissions.se.
Apply through University Admissions, select your programmes and rank them in order of priority - the KTH programme must be first priority.
Pay the application fee of SEK 900 and submit all required documents to University Admissions by the document deadline.

official.application_route: Apply to a KTH master's programme via University Admissions (KTH listed as first priority, fee paid), then submit the KTH India Scholarship form on the scholarship page during the 1 December 2026 - 15 January 2027 window.
official.citizenship_residency: You must be an Indian citizen who has completed your undergraduate programme in India.
official.international_eligibility: Open to fee-paying (non-EU/EEA/Swiss) Indian citizens who completed their undergraduate programme in India; eligibility requires being a fee-paying student, which excludes EU/EEA/Swiss citizens who are generally not required to pay tuition fees.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Not available for applicants to joint master's programmes or programmes with obligatory exchange studies, such as the master's programme in Railway Engineering.

official.description: The KTH India Scholarship Foundation was established in 2012 through a donation made by an anonymous donor, and the foundation is awarding one scholarship in 2027. The scholarship covers the tuition fee for the first and the second year, provided that the study results during the first year are satisfactory, and also includes a monthly living allowance during the academic year (10 months).
official.english_requirement: English proficiency equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6/English Level 2. You can meet the requirement with an English test, for example an overall IELTS score of 6.5 or a TOEFL score of 4.5. Depending on your country of previous studies you could also meet the requirement through completed upper secondary or university studies.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a single-award foundation scholarship for Indian citizens who completed their undergraduate degree in India and who rank a KTH master's programme as their first priority at University Admissions. It removes the tuition fee for both years (the full fee for most two-year programmes is SEK 385,000) and adds a living allowance paid across the 10-month academic year, but KTH does not publish the allowance amount, so plan against KTH's own student budgets of roughly SEK 7,850 to 13,000 per month. The window is short: the form appears on 1 December 2026 and closes on 15 January 2027, with results on 1 April 2027, and admission itself is decided through the separate University Admissions round.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A strong-GPA Indian graduate of a well-ranked Indian university, ideally with Mumbai or Pune connections, who is applying to a standalone KTH master's programme rather than a joint programme.
application_readiness_checklist: Rank the KTH master's programme first on University Admissions before 15 January 2027 - any higher-ranked programme voids scholarship eligibility.
Pay the SEK 900 application fee and upload every required document well before the early-February document deadline.
Bookmark the scholarship page for the application form that appears when the window opens on 1 December 2026; there is no reminder email.
Draft a short account of any Mumbai Metropolitan Area or Pune connection, since the foundation statutes give priority to applicants from those regions.
Confirm your chosen programme is neither a joint programme nor one with obligatory exchange studies, which are excluded outright.
common_rejection_risks: Only one scholarship exists: in 2026, 2 of the 23 admitted scholarship applicants were nominated (9%), so treat it as an upside on top of admission, never as a funding plan.
Listing a KTH programme as second, third or fourth priority in the University Admissions ranking disqualifies you from this scholarship even if you are admitted to it.
Joint programmes and programmes with obligatory exchange studies, such as Railway Engineering, are excluded.
The second-year tuition waiver is conditional on satisfactory study results in the first year.
Applicants who fail the programme's admission requirements are not considered for the scholarship at all.
A missing or late document in the University Admissions file leaves scholarship assessors with nothing to evaluate.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: KTH's 2026 student budgets for Stockholm total SEK 7,850 to 13,000 a month for housing, food, transport, insurance and hobbies, and the example budgets explicitly exclude electricity, internet, phone, course materials, healthcare, household items, clothing, travel, housing deposits and emergencies. The allowance runs for the 10-month academic year only, so the two summer months, the SEK 900 application fee, flights, residence-permit costs and insurance must be funded from other sources.
document_audit: There are no scholarship-specific documents: the whole assessment runs on the University Admissions file, so a poorly uploaded transcript is a poor scholarship application.
Degree documents must follow University Admissions' country instructions for India; final-year students must follow the separate final-year instructions.
The English requirement (English 6, e.g. IELTS 6.5 overall) is assessed from the same file, and a missing result blocks both admission and the scholarship.
The scholarship page states documents are due 2 February while the general how-to-apply page states 1 February - submit before 1 February to be safe.
Do not expect to be asked for a motivation letter, but the criteria include motivation, work experience and extra-curricular activities.
alerts: The application form only exists between 1 December 2026 and 15 January 2027 - about six weeks - and it sits on the same page as this information, not in a separate portal.
You may hold both the KTH India Scholarship and the KTH Scholarship, but the KTH Scholarship covers tuition only and no living allowance.
Neither the allowance amount nor the travel component is published by KTH, so ignore any unofficial SEK figures circulating on aggregator sites and confirm the amount in your offer letter.
Results land on 1 April 2027, the same day as admission results, leaving very little time to arrange a residence permit and funding before the autumn intake.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: First submit a University Admissions application with the KTH programme ranked first and pay the fee, then file the separate KTH India Scholarship form on the scholarship page during the December-January window; KTH assesses admission, then assesses scholarship applicants and announces both on 1 April 2027.
